title: Never gate progress on a background video
statement: Never gate progress on a background video that repeats on-screen teaching, since a required video walls off the learners who most need the lesson.
example: Each unit's background video ran about 56 seconds, and the Next button was live before its first frame played.
detail: A Grade 3 reading build gave each unit one narrated background video of about 56 seconds on the unit's first lesson, after a review found that a child who skips text reaches the passage without the knowledge the level-set screens teach, so the same knowledge is taught again in moving pictures. Its rules never gate progress on watching: the step is informational, so Next is live before a single frame plays. The video never autoplays and plays only from one large child-triggered overlay, and on a load error the frame and its skip button remove themselves, so a missing file degrades to the level-set screens rather than a broken box.
against: A record already there says young learners shouldn't skip or speed up instruction on their own judgment; this video may be passed over only because the same knowledge is taught again on the narrated screens that follow it.

evidence.quote: each UNIT has one ~56s narrated video
so the same knowledge is taught again in moving pictures.
PROGRESS IS NEVER GATED ON WATCHING. The beat is `info:true`, so Next is live before a single frame plays;
A required video is a wall in front of the lesson for exactly the children who most need the lesson.
Never autoplays. Poster frame + one large child-triggered play overlay
On `error` the frame and skip button REMOVE themselves, so a missing mp4 degrades to the level-set screens rather than to a broken box.
